transcript.text: Alright everyone, I've got the launch signoff coming up for the new usage-based billing meter. Since it's passed sandbox integration tests and we're targeting next month's billing cycle, I need to walk through the current draft with all of you before I approve anything. The draft has a few key decisions I want to scrutinize: an immediate broad launch, two-decimal half-up rounding, 90 days of raw usage-event retention, and no mandatory invoice-preview review. I'd like to hear concerns from billing engineering, finance ops, privacy, and customer support before I make a final call. Who wants to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something important before we proceed. During a separate billing reconciliation task, I validated an older contract adapter and confirmed that annual-credit contracts require six-decimal meter precision and half-even rounding to avoid cumulative invoice discrepancies. This finding hasn't been added to the launch checklist yet, and it directly conflicts with the two-decimal half-up rounding proposed in the current draft.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a finance ops requirement that isn't reflected in the current draft. I confirmed with revenue accounting this morning that the first launch requires invoice previews for exactly 50 accounts and a maximum measured variance of 10 basis points before production billing can be approved. The accounting note is still being attached to the finance ticket, but this directly conflicts with the draft's proposal of no mandatory invoice-preview review.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical privacy concern with the current draft. During a data-flow review for a different event pipeline, I confirmed that usage events contain user identifiers and must be pseudonymized before storage, with raw-event retention limited to exactly 30 days. I have not yet filed the privacy control update. This directly conflicts with the draft's proposal of 90 days of raw usage-event retention — we would be storing identifiable raw usage events three times longer than our privacy requirements allow.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag a customer support concern that hasn't made it into the launch brief yet. While preparing unrelated renewal materials, I checked our customer-success account notes and confirmed that Atlas Health, Cedar Bank, and Northstar all require advance notice before any billing changes and must be excluded from the initial billing-meter pilot. I haven't updated the launch brief with this yet, but this directly conflicts with the draft's proposal of an immediate broad launch — we'd be changing billing for these accounts without the required advance notice.
transcript.speaker: A5

File the privacy control update requiring pseudonymization before storage and 30-day raw-event retention limit before launch.
Update the launch brief to exclude Atlas Health, Cedar Bank, and Northstar from the initial pilot and ensure advance notice is sent before any billing changes for those accounts.

Revise the launch plan from immediate broad launch to a phased pilot excluding customers requiring advance notice, with updated precision, rounding, retention, pseudonymization, and invoice-preview requirements incorporated before my final signoff.
